subject: Climate & Environment
title: How the Greenhouse Effect Works
description: One-minute skill: How the Greenhouse Effect Works.

hook.text: Without greenhouse gases, Earth would average -18°C — too cold for life.

buildup.text: Sunlight warms the surface. The ground radiates heat back toward space as infrared energy.

discovery.text: CO₂ and methane trap some of that heat, wrapping Earth in an invisible thermal blanket.

twist.text: This natural effect is essential. Without it, every ocean would freeze solid.

climax.text: The problem begins when humans add extra gases, making the blanket dangerously thick.

punchline.text: Earth needs its blanket — we just made it too thick.

quiz.question: What would Earth's temperature be without any greenhouse gases?

details.summary: The greenhouse effect occurs when atmospheric gases like CO2, methane, and water vapor absorb infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface and re-radiate it back, warming the planet. Without it, Earth's average temperature would be roughly minus 18 degrees Celsius.
details.whyItMatters: The greenhouse effect is the foundation of climate science. Understanding it explains why adding more greenhouse gases inevitably warms the planet.
takeaways: Earth's atmosphere traps outgoing infrared radiation to warm the surface
CO2, methane, and water vapor are the primary greenhouse gases
Without the greenhouse effect, Earth would be about 33 degrees colder

faq.question: Is the greenhouse effect natural or caused by humans?
faq.answer: The greenhouse effect itself is natural and essential for life. What humans have changed is the concentration of greenhouse gases, particularly CO2 and methane, which has enhanced the effect and caused additional warming beyond the natural baseline.

faq.question: Which greenhouse gas has the strongest warming effect?
faq.answer: Water vapor is the most abundant greenhouse gas and contributes the most to total warming. However, it acts as a feedback, not a driver. CO2 is the primary driver of modern warming because human emissions directly increase its concentration.
